claims.on_screen: a proven strategy for reducing this risk

claims.verbatim_source: "Yet prescribed burning remains underused in Alaska because the state lacks weather forecasting tools and community partnerships suited to its unique environment."

claims.on_screen: Prescribed Fire and Smoke Planner / Canadian Forest Fire Weather Index
claims.spoken: a Lower forty eight planner on the index Alaska actually runs
claims.verbatim_source: "This project adapts the Prescribed Fire and Smoke Planner, a decision-support tool already used across the contiguous United States, for use in Alaska by incorporating the Canadian Forest Fire Weather Index system on which Alaska's fire management relies."
claims.label: NSF award abstract

claims.spoken: machine learning reads decades of weather, hunting for the days that would have been safe
claims.verbatim_source: "Using historical weather reanalysis data and statistical and machine-learning techniques, the research team will characterize the geographic and seasonal patterns of hazardous fire weather and identify windows of conditions favorable for safe prescribed burning across Alaska and the broader Northern Pacific Boreal-Arctic region."
claims.label: NSF award abstract

claims.spoken: a borough, a federal agency, a tribal government and a nonprofit
claims.verbatim_source: "governance and land management involve a mix of municipal, federal, Tribal, and non-profit entities"
claims.label: NSF award abstract
claims.note: The VO renders 'municipal' as 'a borough', which is the Alaskan word for that unit. The abstract's own four words are what paint ON SCREEN, so the viewer sees the source language.

claims.verbatim_source: "Educational activities include developing a curriculum for a new four-year wildland fire management program to build capacity among current and future fire professionals."
claims.label: NSF award abstract
claims.note: Cut from the VO for length and carried on screen instead, so the fact survives without spending eight seconds.

claims.verbatim_source: program: "Artificial Intelligence (AI), FIRE-Wildland Fire, INTERDISCIPLINARY PROPOSALS, Improv Undergrad STEM Ed(IUSE), EXP PROG TO STIM COMP RES, UNDERGRADUATE EDUCATION"

claims.on_screen: no liability or insurance provision appears in this award
claims.spoken: who pays when a burn escapes isn't in this award
claims.verbatim_source: A NEGATIVE CLAIM, verified by reading the complete abstractText and the full award record. The words liability, insurance, indemnity and escaped do not occur anywhere in either.
claims.label: verified absence, stated as an absence
claims.note: The film says this is a gap in THIS AWARD, never that Alaska has no liability law. The fair counter-point the angle is required to honor.

cut_by_the_angle_room.what: Tok Fire Prevention Area burn permit suspension, Aug 1 2026
cut_by_the_angle_room.why: CATEGORY ERROR. A burn permit governs a private landowner's debris pile. A prescribed fire is an agency operation under a written prescription. Different activities, different authorities. The irony would have been the film's best hook and it would have been wrong.

cut_by_the_angle_room.what: 52 percent of this season's Alaska wildfires human-caused
cut_by_the_angle_room.why: CATEGORY ERROR. That figure is about ACCIDENTAL ignition. This award is about DELIBERATE ignition. Placing them together invites a viewer to fuse the two and argues against the piece by accident.
NOT USED. It was the one provisional fact the room would have kept if verified, and it is not load-bearing for the thesis. Dropped rather than shipped unverified.

illustrative_note: On-screen counts of burnable days are ILLUSTRATIVE. The project has not run yet and has published no day counts. The film never puts a specific number of burnable days on screen as a finding, and the Gmail draft says so.
